Following the earlier launch of parent-managed accounts for users under 13 this year, WhatsApp today further expanded its parental supervision features to teen accounts, adding group activity notifications and additional restrictions on Meta AI. Details are as follows.

WhatsApp expands parental supervision options

Earlier this year, WhatsApp announced a series of new features designed to give parents greater control over accounts belonging to children under 13.

These include allowing parents to decide who can contact the account, as well as which groups the account can join, viewing message requests from unknown contacts, and managing its privacy settings—all changes protected by a parent-set PIN code.

A few weeks later, WhatsApp further expanded the relevant features on iOS by adding a dedicated "Parental Supervision" tab in the Settings app, making it easier for parents to locate and configure supervised accounts.

WhatsApp today once again expanded its supervision features, this time extending parental supervision from users under 13 to teen users, giving parents greater transparency into their children's group activity, more say in how their children interact with Channels and Status updates, and—most importantly—greater control over their interactions with Meta AI.

With this update, parents can now receive notifications when their child joins or leaves a group, as well as when the number of members in a group they have already joined increases significantly. Parents can also now choose how their children use Channels, whose Status updates they can see, and who can view the content their children post.

As for Meta AI, parents can now choose between the standard experience suitable for users aged 13 and above, or opt for the more restrictive "Limited Content" option, depending on what they deem appropriate for their children.

According to WhatsApp, the "Limited Content" setting will further restrict the topics teens can discuss with Meta AI. When this setting is enabled, Meta AI features that rely on Private Processing technology will also become unavailable.

WhatsApp reiterated that these parental supervision features will not allow parents to read the actual content of their children's messages or calls—communications remain protected by end-to-end encryption.
